text:
ada: Heads-up from a support ticket: Optimize toolkit page has inconsistent SDK examples and a broken internal link. Customer tried the Python snippet and got AttributeError: 'OptimizeClient' object has no attribute 'set_batch'. Link: https://redwood.dev/docs/optimize/toolkit/migration

kyle: Can you paste the exact snippet?

ada: It's under 'Route-level batching + quant' and shows:
```python
client = OptimizeClient()
client.set_batch('route', max_batch=256, timeout_ms=200)
```
But the real API is client.route_config('route').batch(max_size=256, timeout_ms=200) in SDK 1.8+.

nina: Ah, we changed from set_* to route_config helpers in the runtime refactor. This is a docs bug. I can open a PR to update Python and add a short migration callout. Also I noticed the quantization profile example uses the old key "qprofile": "v1" instead of the nested structure we expect now: 
```yaml
quantization:
  profile: "qprofile-v2"
  dtype: "int8"
```
We should link to the qprofiles migration doc.

reza: I can add a Go example too. Also let's add a note about dtype canonicalization: callers might see fp16 in model metadata but should pick int8 or int4 profiles via the new CLI tool. Small note: mention that smaller dtypes with high batch sizes can underflow for some ops.

cal: Quick anchor bug: the anchor for "Route-level batching" moved from #route-batching to #route-level-batching last week (PR #4410) so old permalinks 404. I have a tiny redirect patch ready.

ada: Perfect. Can we also add a bench tip: "start with max_size 16-64 for chat-like short-turn workloads; increase for inference-only bulk jobs" and an explanation about KV cache sizing interplay? Customers hit a pathological throughput drop when they used max_size=1024 with small kv cache.

kyle: Good idea. Add a short snippet showing how to enable prefix caching in Python:
```python
client.route_config('chat').cache(prefix_kv=True, kv_size=64)
```
And mention prefetch heuristics.

docs-bot: PR opened by nina: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4420 - updates Python + Go snippets, adds migration callout, fixes qprofile YAML, and includes anchor redirect. CI running.

ops-bot: linkcheck: /docs/optimize/toolkit/migration -> 404 (before PR).

reza: Quick review: prefer explicit OptimizeClient(...) args in examples so readers know auth and region are required, e.g. OptimizeClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'), region='us-west-2'). Also, add a short compatibility table listing SDK versions and the snippet shapes.

nina: Adding compatibility table and explicit constructor. Also adding a one-liner about behavioral change: route_config helper sets a default timeout of 250ms vs old global default 500ms. We should warn about possible functional differences when migrating.

ada: Can someone backport to release/v1.2 after merge? Dedicated customers still on that doc set.

cal: I'll handle backport and the tiny redirect on release branch.

docs-bot: CI green for PR #4420. Mergeable.

kyle: Merged. Follow-up: I'll open a tracking issue to sweep all optimize pages for old qprofile keys and set up a docs linter rule to flag "qprofile" key usage in YAML.

nina: Thanks team. That should cut down future regressions. Closing ticket on support once backport lands.

ada: :thumbsup:
